data.name: Daaruk
data.gender_notes: Daaruk is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Daaruk is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Daaru’ meaning wood. It is the name of a sage in Hindu mythology, renowned for his strength and valor. He was the architect of the monkey kingdom, 'Kishkindha', and a trusted advisor to Lord Rama. The name Daaruk carries the meaning “Strong, Valiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Daaruk usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, valiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Daaruk belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong, Valiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Daaruk total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Daaruk is a significant name in Indian mythology and folklore, associated with strength, leadership, and architectural prowess. As the architect of 'Kishkindha', Daaruk is known for constructing the beautifully structured and strategically important monkey kingdom, which played a crucial role in the epic Ramayana.
data.spiritual_significance: Daaruk represents the inner strength and perseverance necessary to build not only physical structures but also spiritual foundations. Through his unwavering devotion and loyalty to Lord Rama, he embodies the ideals of duty, truth, and sacrifice that continue to inspire and guide Hindu spiritual practices.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Daaruk is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Daru', meaning a tree or wood. In Hindu mythology, Daruk is also known for his devotion towards Lord Hanuman. His name symbolizes strength, durability, and unwavering faith.
